calibration.note: Four street-plane points confirmed by hand on frame 0 (540x960 display coordinates, pan-stabilised to frame 0): the near curb line and the first lane line of 7th Ave. Length from the taxi in frame (4.9 m long, ~200 px); width is one standard NYC lane (3.0 m, assumption).

events.note: Three yellow taxis and a black SUV occupy the lanes in front of the theater.
A line of yellow taxis is stopped or crawling along the avenue beneath the billboards.
Dozens of people walk and stand in the illuminated pedestrian plaza.
Large crowd fills the plaza and walkways in front of the billboards.
Crowd gathers and walks through the plaza below the large video screens.
People sit closely together on the red steps watching the area.
People sit and stand on the steps with no roadway interaction visible.

totals.summary: The camera pans across Times Square at night from the Palace Theatre toward crowded pedestrian plazas and billboards. No pedestrians were seen entering the active roadway and vehicle traffic consisted of queued taxis with no turning conflicts observed.

concepts.why: Lines the curb between the sidewalk and taxi lanes and narrows walking space while keeping crowds from spilling into traffic.
Tall pole standing in the middle of pedestrian flow is a collision obstacle and blocks sightlines between walkers and drivers.
Tiered seating area where crowds sit and climb creates trip, slip, and fall risk in dense foot traffic.
Low transparent barrier around the stepped terrace prevents falls but is hard to see and can channel or trap crowds.
Short protective posts separate the pedestrian plaza from vehicle lanes and both protect walkers and obstruct the walkway.

method.near_miss: post-encroachment time < 1.5 s between a walker and a vehicle at the crosswalk
method.risk: near-misses weighted by (vehicle speed / 9 m/s)^2, a kinetic-energy proxy

effects.lpi: walkers start crossing lpi_s seconds before turning cars are released; drivers see walkers already in the crosswalk more easily (+4 pts detection)
effects.hardened_centerline: rubber curbs and posts at the centre line force a tighter, slower left turn: turning speed x0.75, +3 pts detection (assumption)
effects.daylighting: removing parking next to the crosswalk opens the sightline: +5 pts detection for turning drivers, +2 pts for through drivers (assumption)
effects.turn_ban: banned avenue turns move to the next downstream street that runs the same way; drivers comply at ban_compliance (default 90%, assumption); each diverted car adds ~40 s of detour (assumption)
effects.split_phase: turning cars get their own interval after the parallel walk and flashing DON'T WALK end, so turns never share the walk

coordinator.plan_note: Priorities blend simulated risk with 2023-26 pedestrian casualties, so some corners are elevated on real history where the two diverge (notably W 33, W 36, W 47, W 53, W 56) and purely simulated hotspots are retained where real crashes are fewer (W 46). stress.why: The plan concentrates spending in the theatre-area cluster at w42, w43, w45 and w46. A simultaneous show-out pedestrian surge could overwhelm the LPIs and crosswalks there and increase turning conflicts beyond the weekday 5-6 pm test condition.

stress.label: Rain at night
stress.why: Most accepted protection is visibility- and timing-based: daylighting, LPIs and hardened centre lines. Rain at night reduces visibility and lengthens braking distances, weakening those measures while making near-misses more likely.
